title: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
methods: linear probes on mean-pooled residual stream (SigLIP, Gemma, action expert)
shuffled-label control task with MLP capacity sweep
probe-residual OOD detector vs Mahalanobis, VAE, SAFE-MLP/LSTM
question: Is task progress (normalized time remaining) linearly readable from pi0.5's activations, does it respond to language, can it steer the policy, and is it useful as a label-free OOD monitor?
key_findings: Progress is linearly decodable from early layers: layer-0 Gemma probe R2 = 0.95 in-distribution; also decodable in early SigLIP layers (Fig. 2).
A large true-vs-shuffled-label gap holds across MLP probe capacities, so decodability is selective (Fig. 2 right, no numbers in text).

Feature is observable in PaliGemma but the three pi0.x variants 'substantially outperform' it and are comparable to each other: attributed to robot pretraining, not fine-tuning (Fig. 3, 400 train / 50 held-out episodes per task).

The naive layer-0 probe ignores language (output unchanged under noun swap). A layer-10 probe trained with counterfactuals labelled tau=1.0 becomes language-sensitive but in-distribution R2 drops to 0.33.
Not steerable: injecting tau_boost=0.2 at layer 0 does not change probe readouts at layers 1-17, and injected actions stay far from the future ground-truth actions (5 demos x 5 injections).
OOD detection (cross-task, AUROC): per-replan V_tau 0.796 seen / 0.833 unseen vs SAFE-MLP 0.917 / 0.935; per-episode V_tau 0.910 / 0.851 vs SAFE-MLP 0.904 / 0.917 (Table 1).
Cross-perturbation (held-out noise modes): V_tau per-episode 0.960 vs SAFE-MLP 0.894 and SAFE-LSTM 0.857 on unseen modes (Table 2).
Appendix: the fine-tuned pi0.5 ignores the instruction. Under a prompt swap it reaches for the original target in 10/10 episodes, and after a position swap it grasps the relocated target in 3/18.

evidence.scale: probes: 400 train / 50 held-out episodes per task; OOD: 300 ID trajectories over 6 tasks, 50 OOD trajectories per task per noise mode per injection point, 4 noise modes x 3 injection points; 20 task splits; steering: 5 demos x 5 injections; probe seed 42
evidence.statistics: partial: AUROC mean +/- std over splits; 95% CI bands over 75 rollouts in Fig. 4 and over 5x5 injections in Fig. 5; no significance tests
evidence.baselines: Mahalanobis, VAE, SAFE-MLP, SAFE-LSTM for OOD; shuffled-label control for probing; PaliGemma and base pi0.5 for emergence

causal_validation: Yes, and the result is negative: injection along the layer-0 probe direction does not propagate to later-layer probes and does not move actions toward the counterfactual future actions. Only one layer, one direction and one magnitude were tested.
closed_loop: Mixed. OOD detection uses closed-loop rollouts with perturbations injected online. Steerability is measured open-loop as action distance on demonstration frames, not by rolling out the steered policy.
limitations_stated: Progress is normalized time in successful demos, conflating elapsed time with semantic completion.
Counterfactual labels (tau=1.0 for swapped prompts) are proxies.
Negative steering result is narrow: single direction, single layer, fixed magnitude.
critique: A progress probe at layer 0 (R2 0.95), also present in SigLIP, most likely reads arm pose and scene configuration from the image. That is a visual-progress cue, not evidence of a policy-internal 'value' representation. The non-steerability fits this reading: changing a layer-0 visual summary need not alter later computation along the same direction.

Testing steering at layer 0, where the probe is most 'visual', is the weakest place to test whether the policy uses progress. Mid-layer injections were not run, so 'progress is not steerable' is not established in general.

The OOD perturbations are synthetic image corruptions (noise, blur, colour shift, occlusion). Detecting stalled progress under these is easier than detecting semantic or physical failures, so the advantage over SAFE on unseen modes may not carry over to natural failures.

Abstract says the signal is 'present in the pretrained PaliGemma backbone', while Sec. 4.2 says it is 'established by large-scale robotic pre-training'. These are reconcilable (weak in PaliGemma, strong after robot pretraining) but the framing is inconsistent.
Valuable side finding: the VLABench-fine-tuned pi0.5 ignores language (10/10 prompt swaps), which matches the 'encoded but not used' theme in 2610.06235 and 2607.03372.
one_line: Task progress can be read linearly from pi0.5's earliest layers and works as a label-free OOD monitor competitive with supervised detectors, but pushing activations along the progress direction does not change the policy.
